title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving nutritional assistance to vulnerable and hard-to-reach communities in Diinsoor District, Bay Region, Somalia.

description.narrative: ltpgtSalama Medical Agency (SAMA) proposes to implement a 12-month emergency nutrition project in Dinsoor District, Bay Region, Somalia, with a total budget of USD 300,000.69 funded by the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF). The project seeks to reduce acute malnutrition and associated mortality among vulnerable populations, particularly children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs), through an integrated package of facility- and community-based nutrition services. The intervention will directly target 15,000 individuals across high-need locations, including Jambal Awes, Jileelow, Waberi, Saakow IDP, and Korkamari IDP settlements.ltbrgtThe proposed intervention will respond to the growing humanitarian needs driven by recurrent droughts, flooding, crop failure, and rising food prices, which have weakened household resilience and disrupted access to essential services. A recent nutrition survey conducted by SAMA in March 2025 confirmed a deteriorating food security and nutrition situation in Dinsoor, compounded by the suspension of critical programs due to funding gaps. This project aims to close these gaps and ensure that the most affected communities receive lifesaving nutrition assistance.ltbrgtSAMA will pursue five key outcomes under this project. First, the project will strengthen early detection and referral of acute malnutrition by conducting six rounds of mass MUAC and oedema screening and training 400 caregivers on the Family MUAC approach. Additionally, 20 community health workers (CHWs) will be trained to conduct regular screenings, referrals, and community awareness activities, increasing early identification and access to treatment.ltbrgtSecond, the project will improve access to treatment for severe acute malnutrition (SAM) through two fixed OTP sites and three outreach teams. These teams will operate across five target locations to provide weekly services. SAMA will admit and treat 1,500 children with SAM and refer complicated cases to stabilization centers. The project will also train 26 health and nutrition workers in Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM), incorporating child protection and disability inclusion.ltbrgtThird, the project will promote optimal infant and young child feeding (IYCF) and maternal nutrition practices. SAMA will provide IYCF counseling to 2,500 caregivers, conduct monthly community education sessions, and facilitate cooking demonstrations. The First Foods campaign, promoting one egg per day, will be rolled out alongside the establishment of 24 care groups and training for 40 workers on MIYCAN/IYCF.ltbrgtFourth, SAMA will improve the nutritional status of children and PLWs through micronutrient supplementation. The project will deliver Vitamin A to 3,000 children, distribute MNPs to 2,000 children under two, and provide MMS or iron-folic acid to 3,000 PLWs via fixed and mobile services.ltbrgtFifth, the project will integrate protection throughout all activities. This includes 12 community feedback sessions, training 20 staff on PSEA, GBV, and child protection, and monthly awareness sessions on aid diversion prevention. Market monitoring will help detect and address misuse of supplies.ltbrgtThe project will run from July 2025 to July 2026, with monthly implementation and quarterly supervision. SAMA will coordinate with the Nutrition Cluster and government partners and use standard monitoring tools to ensure timely reporting and quality implementation.ltbrgtlt/pgt
